text: The rwb-document capability uses the per-service database login of DP-02; the story refers to "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and never to a shared login
why: DP-02 fixes one login per service but no source names it; the app story needs a login to build and test against
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 4 and slide 8; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02
confirm: ACE DB team names the login in the rwb_document DB story
impact: No build blocker: the login is configured per environment; the placeholder keeps the story free of a shared-login assumption

text: The containers rwb-docs, rwb-docs-legal and rwb-quarantine, the path {container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1 and the managed identity are carried from the legacy story; the storage account and the immutability policy belong to RWB-PLT-TE012-APP
why: The legacy story fixes the three containers and the path, the architecture fixes Blob with WORM, and no source fixes the account or the policy period
read: Legacy story RWB-E1-024 sections 3, 4 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 16
confirm: SCB IT infrastructure confirms the account, the container names per environment and the WORM policy in RWB-PLT-TE012-APP
impact: The store can be built and tested against the storage product stub and the SIT containers; a policy change touches configuration only

text: The five store operations keep the paths of the target REST base, answer with the TSD P5 Document shape, and answer a missing document with an RFC 9457 problem response whose message ID is left to the contract story
why: The TSD fixes the operations, the authorization and the error codes but not every field name or the 404 message ID; the story needs a shape to build against
read: TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16; Template and Rules v1 R9
confirm: Solution architect publishes the OpenAPI for the five operations with the request and response field names and the not-found message ID
impact: The service builds against the TSD shape and its fake; a field-name change is a contract version change, not a redesign

text: The three case documents operations keep the legacy request and response intent, and their field names will be published by a P5 contract; until then the story uses the legacy item names (Document, DocumentPage, DocumentChecklist) and the per-service login is referred to as "the rwb-document login (DP-02)".
why: RWB-E1-026 is a moved story, so its behaviour is carried unchanged, and the plan has no P5 CON story for this key; the split plan and the WP give no contract for these paths, and the login name is absent from every source.
read: TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A (API-P5-001, API-P5-002, API-P5-008) and Template and Rules v1 DP-02, DP-13
confirm: Solution architect, before the contract tests of wave 1
impact: Sections 12.1 and 14 are rewritten against the published contract; no business behaviour changes.

text: The scan of RWB-P5-E1041-CON is called as one published operation after the intake container write and before the store, with a 2 s budget, an answer of CLEAN or INFECTED, and no store call on any other answer.
why: The order scan-then-store is a business rule (BR2, REQ-DCM-010) in every source, but the interface that carries it is not specified; the one-hop REST budget of Architecture v5 slide 11 is the only shape the sources give.
read: FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.18 and AC-BG-P5-001-01; Architecture v5 slide 11 and slide 16
confirm: Owner of RWB-P5-E1041-CON before build step 2
impact: The scan call site in CaseDocumentUploadService changes if the contract differs; the order and the refusal stay.

text: SCR-30 is served only through the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON, which calls this service one hop for the list, the upload and the checklist and merges the answer; the browser is never given the service base path.
why: DP-19 and Architecture v5 slide 10 fix the one-hop rule and the route owner, but the route path and the merged screen model are not written in any source.
read: Template and Rules v1 DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 10 (documents tab) and slide 11 (one hop, 2 s)
confirm: Owner of RWB-PLT-N001-CON before the SIT browser test
impact: Section 15 and build step 6 name the published route; the service operations do not change.

text: The trigger event rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 is built with the payload fields documentId, caseId, documentType, source and storedAt, all IDs and codes with no personal data, and it is validated against the JSON schema registered for the P5 topic under BACKWARD compatibility; the field names are taken from TSD P5 T3.1 and Architecture v5 slide 16 until a P5 contract baseline fixes them
why: The event is produced and tested in this slice but no CON story of this run owns the producer-side AsyncAPI document and JSON schema of rwb.document.events.v1, so the field list has to be stated from the technical specification and the architecture contract slide
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 and slide 16; TSD P5 v2 T3.1, T5.3; FSD P5 v3 A2.1 AC-P5-001-01; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-09, DP-14
confirm: Solution architect and the platform event team confirm the registered schema before the SIT trigger run
impact: No build block: the factory and the contract test bind to the schema name and fail on a rename; a schema change before registration is a fixture change, not a code change

text: rwb-document connects with one login of its own that holds rights in schema rwb_document only and no privilege on another schema; the login name and the grants are agreed in the database story of the epic
why: Template and Rules v1 §R4 and DP-02 fix one login per service but no source document gives the name, the grant set or the secret reference for rwb-document
read: Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 and slide 8 notes
confirm: ACE database administrator confirms the login name and grants
impact: No build block: the login is a secret reference and a grant script; the stories use the phrase "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" until the database story lands

text: The case binding uses the per-service database login of DP-02, referred to as "the rwb-document login (DP-02)"; a case the rwb-case contract does not return, or does not answer for inside the 2 s budget, is refused with 404 and the contract's not-found message, whose ID is left to RWB-P3-E1018-CON; the case read carries the case ID and the case number of the contract answer and no other case value is read
why: DP-02 fixes one login per service and DP-11 fixes a one-hop contract read, but no source names the login, the not-found message ID or the case-read field names, and the story cannot build or test the refusal without deciding them
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 4, 8 and 16; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02 and DP-11, R9; legacy story RWB-E1-018 sections 12 and 14; TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A
confirm: The solution architect and the ACE DB team fix the login, the case-read field names and the not-found message ID in RWB-P3-E1018-CON and the rwb_document DB story
impact: No build blocker: the login is configuration per environment, the binding builds against the published fake, and a later message ID or field-name change is a contract version change, not a redesign

text: P5 serves the document-type load, the approve and the in-force read at /api/recovery/document/v1/admin/document-types/loads, .../loads/{loadId}/approve and /document-types, with the field shapes and the load template columns to be published in the rwb-document OpenAPI document before the wave-1 harness
